purpose: Ordinary packaging provenance for this Cube-owned editable subtree; not a runtime schema, registry, kernel identity or grant of authority

shared_carrier.adaptation: finite local-only carrier, not new window design

kernel.acceptance_note: Latest accepted Installer main generation after #18 and #21; Cube vendored kernel remains byte-identical. Package payload delivery remains distinct from Cube/Sphere native mathematical format.
kernel.currentness_rule: Vendored kernel must match latest accepted Installer main generation; a newer lane report about an older merged PR cannot downgrade currentness.

published_dev4.status: immutable historical binary; editable integration rebuild is not automatic artifact promotion

acceptance_gaps: authenticated broker and native ports binding
inherited_donor_portability_debt: Exact pinned CLI/connection source retains historical Aries/Loki profile names, help text and device aliases. Native packaging does not use these strings as portable defaults, installation targets or authority. Any donor cleanup belongs upstream and requires repinning/requalification, not silent local source edits.

cube_native_model.meaning: Reusable XI-IO project/product structure and native mathematical representation; not an OS package or customer host layout

recursive_composition.rule: A Cube may contain or reference child Cubes recursively. Parent/child composition expresses reusable product/project structure, not customer ownership or runtime authority.
examples: XI-IO Studio -> Desktop -> WordPress plugin Cube

black_box.rule: Each Cube owns its reusable work-enablement package for that Cube/repository: scripts, skills, regression and acceptance tests, product-local manifests/settings, and stable agent/role assignment references needed to perform work. Black Box contains capability definitions and references, never customer credentials or implicit effect authority.

sphere_native_model.meaning: User/customer-specific persistent data and native mathematical representation; survives payload replacement and is never embedded as donor-machine literals

cross_cube_scope.rule: A User Sphere is a user/customer data and relationship domain that may relate to many top-level and nested Cubes. It is not duplicated merely because a user uses another Cube.
examples: one User Data Sphere relates to VeilRIFT Cubes
the same User Data Sphere relates to XI-IO Studio product Cubes
cross_cube_scope.custody: BINS owns resource identity, versions, provenance and storage bindings; Sphere records governed relationships rather than copying payload files.

customer_connections.rule: Sphere carries the customer's provisioned identities, connection bindings, account relationships, preferences, billing/provisioning relationship and BINS resource references used across all authorized Cubes. Secrets remain in authorized secret/custody providers, not copied into Cube manifests.

payload_delivery.meaning: Built, immutable platform delivery artifact selected and installed by HEX; packaging is separate from Cube/Sphere mathematical serialization

node_runtime.meaning: Qualified running materialization of an admitted Cube plus authorized Sphere on a real target; installed bytes alone do not create a Node

interaction_seam.rule: Create/register a Node when software from a Cube is installed/running and interacts with an authorized Sphere on a qualified runtime. A directory relationship alone is not a Node.
requirements: BINS-backed user resource custody where persistent user data is read or written

relationship_graph.model: Cube hierarchy is recursive; Sphere bindings are independent many-to-many graph edges; Node materializes an authorized Cube/Sphere interaction on a qualified runtime.

glass_box.rule: Glass Box is the governed projection across the Cube/Sphere seam. It exposes portable capability schemas from the Cube Black Box together with current per-user/per-worker Sphere connection state, while resolving currentness, qualification and authority for each operation. It is not a credential store and does not grant authority by being visible.

global_admin_projection.rule: Provisioning, connected-account administration and metered billing are shared framework capabilities projected as reusable widgets/surfaces into every applicable product Cube. Products consume the common contract; they do not fork customer/account/billing implementations.
requirements: provisioned login resolves one Sphere/principal context
connected provider/account relationships resolve from Sphere state
metering is scoped to admitted product/service usage
billing consent and spending limits precede paid effects
BINS/resource custody references remain independently read back
widget availability does not imply provider or billing authority
